Subject: Acme Financial — tenant-level audit export requirement (deal contingency)

Team,

Quick summary: Acme is asking for a per-tenant/contract-level audit export (syslog/S3 deliverable) that includes full request/response logs, prompts and metadata, and an immutable export retention window. Procurement has put this as a gating item for signature — they will not sign unless we either deliver the feature or accept a contractual exception documented in the SOW. Deal context: $1.2M ARR committed if we meet the pilot date and compliance asks (see attached MAP).

Asks:
- Product: can we scope a minimum viable export (schema + delivery) that satisfies Acme's security/compliance team? They care about encryption-at-rest, per-tenant isolation, and a retention policy they can audit.
- Eng (Laura): rough feasibility + ETA for a pilot-grade export (no UI required; S3 push + manifest acceptable). Flag any infra/security blockers.
- CS (Monica): what evidence will Acme accept for SOC2/PII handling while we build?

Acme timeline: pilot by Oct 1, production by Jan 1. Rishi is on the thread with the contract details; procurement has attached a redline.

Attachments: 2026-07-15-Acme-MAP.pdf, Acme-contract-redline-v2.docx

I want a short reply with feasibility + a single owner for the RFC by EOD July 27. This is high impact — if we can get a clear path, we keep the deal.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Acme Financial — tenant-level audit export requirement (deal contingency)

Jonas—thanks for the heads up. High level thoughts:

1) Two implementation patterns we can offer:
   - Batch/object export: periodic manifest + gzipped JSONL pushed to customer-owned S3 or a RedCloud bucket with per-tenant prefixes. Easier to audit, simpler to meet retention.
   - Streaming webhook/forwarder: near-real-time delivery to a URL; requires signed delivery and replay guarantees.

2) Minimum viable: batch/object export (S3) with encryption (KMS), per-tenant prefixing, manifest including checksums and sequence numbers. This avoids realtime guarantees and keeps scope smaller.

3) Non-functional requirements we need from Acme: retention duration (they asked 7 years in the call?), residency (US-only?), allowed personnel access list, and whether raw prompt text is allowed to be exported or must be redacted/anonymized.

4) Rough effort: scoped pilot for S3 push ~ 6–8 engineer-weeks: one infra engineer (storage & delivery), one backend (export pipeline + manifest), one security engineer (KMS & compliance hooks). From product side: a short RFC + acceptance criteria. If we include redaction/anonymization as part of scope, add 2–3 weeks.

5) Risks: export of raw prompts increases PII risk and will trigger additional legal/compliance review; long retention increases storage cost and potential eDiscovery burden.

Next steps (my recommendation):
- Confirm the data elements Acme requires (full transcript vs metadata only).
- Create SUP-1584 (engineering ticket) with a minimal RFC template (owner: Dev).
- Product to propose acceptance criteria and pilot acceptance checklist by July 27.

I can own the RFC doc if someone from Eng volunteers to own the implementation ticket.

—Dev

Subject: Re: Acme Financial — tenant-level audit export requirement (deal contingency)

Thanks — I want to call out a few engineering constraints and proposed mitigations.

Constraints:
- Per-tenant isolation + CMK requirement means each export job must be policy-checked against tenant metadata and the KMS key store. This is doable, but we need an SRE/ops plan for key rotation and key access auditing.
- 7-year retention is significant; we currently don't have a built-in archival lifecycle for export blobs tied to contract-level retention. We'll need a lifecycle policy + cost estimate.
- Performance: exporting full request/response including embeddings payload will dramatically increase object size and cost; need to agree which fields are mandatory.

Proposed mitigations:
- Pilot scope: S3 object export, customer-supplied bucket optionally, KMS-encrypted objects, manifest file with checksums and sequence ids. No realtime delivery for pilot.
- Implement feature flag + per-tenant config so we can enable only for Acme during pilot.
- Start with a redaction toggle: allow CS to redact user identifiers in the pilot. Full raw text export deferred to phase 2 after SOC/legal sign-off.

I'll raise SUP-1584 and add architecture notes; estimate earliest pilot-ready build start = mid-September if we get RFC by July 27 and approvals for CMK access and residency.

Questions for Sales/Product:
- Can Acme accept pilot with redaction on PII?
- Who owns KMS key provisioning and who will be the contact at Acme for Service Account and S3 permissions?

—Laura
